summary: George R. Elder is a scholar in Buddhist studies and Tibetology. He studied at Columbia University under doctoral supervisor Alex Wayman (attested 1978).
George Rupp is a scholar of religious studies and philosophy who studied at Princeton, Yale, and Harvard. He held posts at Rice University (1985–1993) and Columbia University (~1993–2002).
George Saintsbury studied at King's College School and Merton College (~1863–1868). He later held an academic post at the University of Edinburgh (~1895–1915).

George Santayana was a philosopher who studied at Harvard, Berlin, and Cambridge, earning his PhD at Harvard under William James. He served on the philosophy faculty at Harvard University from 1907 to 1912.
George Shirt was an Indologist and linguist. He earned a B.A. from the University of Cambridge by 1864 and studied at the Church Missionary Society College, Islington (~1864–1866).

George Thibaut, an Indologist who studied under Albrecht Weber, served as director of Sampurnanand Sanskrit University, principal of Muir Central College and Sanskrit College, and registrar at the universities of Allahabad and Calcutta.
George Thomas Staunton was a sinologist who studied at Trinity College, Cambridge (~1797–1798). He served as Vice-President of the Royal Asiatic Society of Great Britain and Ireland (~1823–1859).

George Turnour was a scholar in Indology, Buddhist studies, and history/archaeology. He served in the Ceylon Civil Service as a Member of the Supreme Council (1818) and Assistant to the Commissioner of Revenue (1820).

George Uglow Pope worked in Indology and linguistics. He founded and headed both Breeks Memorial School and Bishop Cotton Boys' School, and later served as Lecturer in Tamil at the University of Oxford (~1884–1907).

George V. Bobrinskoy was an Indologist and linguist who studied at Lutheran Theological Seminary and under Franklin Edgerton at Yale. He spent his career at the University of Chicago, serving as linguistics department chair from 1951 to 1966.

George Watt studied medicine at the universities of Aberdeen and Glasgow. He served as professor of botany at Presidency College/Presidency University and held positions at the University of Calcutta, the Indian Museum, and the University of Edinburgh.

George de Roerich studied at Harvard, London, and Paris under scholars including Sylvain Lévi and Charles Rockwell Lanman. He directed the Urusvati Himalayan Research Institute (~1930–1942) and headed a department at the Institute of Oriental Studies (~1957–1960).

George van Driem is a linguist and Tibetologist who studied at Virginia and Leiden. He held professorial chairs at Leiden University (1996–1999, ~2001–2009) and served as Professor of Historical Linguistics at the University of Bern (2010–2022).

Georges B. J. Dreyfus is a scholar of Buddhist studies, Tibetology, and philosophy. He earned a Geshe degree at Ganden Shartse Monastery, completed a PhD at the University of Virginia under Jeffrey Hopkins, and became a professor at Williams College.

Georges Dumézil was a scholar of linguistics, religious studies, and Indology who studied under Antoine Meillet. He held posts at Istanbul, Uppsala, and Warsaw before teaching at EPHE (~1933–1968) and holding a chair at Collège de France (1949–1968).

Georges Perrot was an archaeologist and historian who studied at the École Normale Supérieure. He later held posts at the École Pratique des Hautes Études and the University of Paris, and served as director of the École Normale Supérieure (~1883–1903).
Georges Sorel was a philosopher who was educated at Collège-lycée Jacques-Decour and studied at École polytechnique (~1865–1867).

Georges-Jean Pinault is a linguist and Indologist who studied at ENS, Sorbonne Nouvelle, and EPHE under Jean Haudry. He taught at Sorbonne Nouvelle and Clermont Auvergne before becoming a professor at EPHE in 1999.

Georgios T. Halkias, a scholar of Buddhist studies and Tibetology, completed his DPhil at Oxford under Charles Ramble. He held research posts at SOAS, the Warburg Institute, and Bochum before joining the University of Hong Kong (~2013).

Gerald Hüther studied at the University of Leipzig (~1969–1974). He held posts at the Max Planck Institute for Experimental Medicine (1979–1989) and Universitätsmedizin Göttingen / University of Göttingen (~1994–2016).
